audit: 2026-09-17 scheduled remote agent, fifth fire of the day: one 43 question batch across all four modules, published as data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-17_e_01.json through e_05.json, split into five files for reliable transfer through the GitHub MCP. Split 9 Paediatrics, 10 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 12 Psychiatry and 12 Medicine; tier mix 17 L3, 25 L4 and 1 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 7022 with the four modules at 1754, 1755, 1756 and 1757. CELL SELECTION: this fire adopted the denominator established by the fourth fire, measuring each tier against the achievable L3 to L5 stock rather than a whole topic denominator that still holds 353 to 422 permanently unreachable legacy L2 questions per module. Under the literal reading every L3 and L4 cell shows a double digit deficit that can never close and the raw argmax degenerates: a strict simulation of the per question rule allocated 48 of 50 questions to L3 and dropped Psychiatry entirely. Measured over the achievable tiers the starting shares were Paediatrics 49.12/44.14/6.74, Obstetrics 49.17/44.17/6.67, Psychiatry 49.31/44.32/6.37 and Medicine 49.22/44.18/6.60, so L3 and L4 were each 0.7 to 0.9 points short while L5 was 1.4 to 1.7 points in surplus in every module. The batch was therefore steered to L4 as the deficient tier and L5 held to a single item, and two Medicine drafts initially rated L5, the hepatorenal syndrome albumin challenge item and the pulmonary embolism item with an absolute contraindication to systemic lysis, were rated down to L4 under the standing instruction to rate down when unsure. Final shares are Paediatrics 49.16/44.14/6.70, Obstetrics 49.10/44.29/6.62, Psychiatry 49.17/44.44/6.39 and Medicine 49.08/44.38/6.54: L4 improved in all four modules and the L5 surplus fell in all four. DUPLICATE CONTROL, third consecutive confirmation of the gate weakness: scripts/dupe_gate.py passed the first assembled batch of 50 cleanly with 0 of 50 duplicates, but the separate answer axis screen the fourth fire recommended flagged 21 of those 50, of which 18 were judged substantive repeats testing an identical exam point and were withdrawn. Examples include a periodic fever item scoring 0.924 on the answer axis against paed-0915d-07, heavy menstrual bleeding against sched-2026-09-07-p1a-019 at 0.820, gout in renal impairment against sched-0915b-med-002 at 0.818, long acting injectable transition against sched-0917b-psych-018 at 0.778 and the lithium anti-inflammatory interaction against sched-0917d-psy-005 at 0.769; in every case the combined score was far below the gate threshold because subtopic_detail wording differed while the tested decision was the same. Thirteen replacements were written from ideas pre-screened on the answer axis, an exercise with 42 per cent yield across 26 candidate ideas, and two of those thirteen still flagged on final wording and were also withdrawn, leaving 43. That last point is a method note worth recording: pre-screening must use the exact final option text, because approximate draft wording scored an acute otitis media item at 0.592 and a sleep study item at 0.544 that finished at 0.759 and 0.929 once written. Three residual flags were retained after review as phrase collisions across genuinely different conditions rather than repeats: cholestasis birth timing against a vasa praevia item, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura against a hyperviscosity item, and bacterial tracheitis against an irritable hip item, each sharing only a generic action phrase. RECOMMENDATION for the maintainer, now supported by three independent fires: add an answer only rule to scripts/dupe_gate.py firing at about 0.62 regardless of subtopic_detail similarity, with a guard so that pairs whose details are unrelated are surfaced for review rather than hard failed, since three of the flags this run were legitimate. Without that change the gate will keep reporting clean batches that contain near duplicates, and at roughly 1755 questions per module the common Year 4 curriculum is saturated enough that this is now the binding constraint on batch size rather than generation capacity. Clusters published include paediatric prolonged jaundice and the conjugated fraction, spiral tibial fracture against inflicted injury, salt wasting congenital adrenal hyperplasia, bacterial tracheitis, developmental dysplasia imaging timing, osteosarcoma biopsy siting, obstetric cholestasis birth timing, placenta accreta spectrum, uterine inversion, uterine rupture in labour, Sheehan syndrome, mechanical valve preconception anticoagulation, Turner syndrome presenting as primary amenorrhoea, recurrent miscarriage investigation, clozapine free intervals, catatonia, lithium nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and lithium toxicity with a mistimed level, bipolar depression, Lewy body antipsychotic sensitivity, refeeding phosphate, stimulant cardiac screening, grief against depression, euglycaemic ketoacidosis, subacute combined degeneration, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, hepatorenal syndrome, hypothermic cardiac arrest, drug induced liver injury, adrenal sick day rules and vancomycin dosing in acute kidney injury. NOTE: 62 legacy L1 questions remain in the bank, 18 Paediatrics, 18 Obstetrics, 10 Psychiatry and 16 Medicine, mostly in the original questions_*.json seed files.
